summary: The support and new log-affine root law are complete, full-rank, correctly normalized, and have equal original fiber masses. Tightness of any affine-normalized convergent root subsequence bounds the long fiber's diameter and forces the short fiber's diameter to vanish. The resulting subsequential representations of both the root and canonical laws follow from uniform-grid convergence, preserve the original parity-mixture normalization, and contain an atom of mass at least one half. This excludes every stated reference measure with positive continuous dimension. The two concrete normalizations and the ordinary-midpoint atom comparison are correct. The width-one separation applies to the new original law with the exact predecessor normalization and yields the stated total-variation and KL bounds. No mathematical error or gap was found.
